programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: "The phones"Bluey and Bingo want to play at the restaurant with grandfather but the game is not what the old man expected. He's gonna need an app.
programme.desc-more: This funny and sincere look at modern family life celebrates how creative games help to shape children. Bluey, an Australian puppy-poy, has a mind-blowing imagination and loves to turn daily life into fun adventures. She and her little sister Bingo are embarking on exploring their world, using the game to overcome their fears and try to play adult roles. They are more pleased with nothing than to train their parents, especially their father, in their games. Mom, Chilli, went back to work, and Dad, Bandit, juggles between child care and telework. But if he thinks he's the one who commands it, it's the girls who lead the dance when it comes to playing, but also for everything else!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: "The furniture in kit" While Dad and Mom are putting up their new ratchet in a garden kit, Bluey and Bingo use the packaging board and the wrapping paper to create their own micro-civilization.
programme.desc-more: In the colorful and sparkling world of Bluey, a young blue bitch, the daily adventure takes a playful and imaginative turn. Accompanied by her little sister Bingo, Bluey transforms everyday situations into captivating games. When Bluey receives an invitation to a birthday party, the excitement is at its peak. However, Bingo, with his magical pen, complicates the preparations by introducing unexpected and fanciful elements that test the patience of the whole family. At the same time, their father, Bandit (David McCormack), is confronted with the challenges of daily life when he has to drive his daughters to school. The two little bitches, with their overly creativeness, will not fail to imagine hilarious and surprising scenarios, making each moment memorable. Through games that reflect their daily lives, Bluey and Bingo learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and imagination, while bringing joy and laughter to those around them.

programme.title: Simon Superlapin
programme.desc: "You won't catch us! Super Rabbit and Super Lou want to play wolf. But today, Professor Wolf is not in the mood to want to catch little rabbits. He's all sad.
programme.desc-more: In this captivating episode of Simon Superlapin, Simon (Simon Superlapin) and his group of friends discover an unexpected facet of the world of wolves. While Professor Wolf, the well-known antagonist, embodies the threat, Grandma Wolf and her granddaughter Bonnie reveal another reality. Grandma Wolf, a big-hearted wolf, is a valuable ally, able to defuse tensions and show that not all wolves share the same malicious intentions. Bonnie (Bonnie), for her part, showed surprising courage in protecting her rabbit friends from the constant attacks of her cousin. Turning into a Super Nini, she deploys unsuspecting talents to defend those she loves. This episode highlights the themes of loyalty and understanding, while reminding us that appearance can often be misleading. Simon and his band will learn that even in a world full of dangers, friendship can arise from the most unexpected places.

programme.title: Simon Superlapin
programme.desc: "I'm the one who's been wolfing" Even the naughty Professor Wolf can be a little nervous! He's got a show for Grandma Wolf and as he's afraid, he's forcing Super Ferdi to replace him, otherwise he'll chew him!
programme.desc-more: In this captivating episode of season 2 of "Simon Superlapin", the excitement is at its peak as Simon (voice of the actor), Lou (voice of the actor) and Ferdinand (voice of the actor) prepare to present a show in front of all the parents. Costumes and energy overflowing, the three friends are determined to deliver a memorable performance. However, pressure rises when Ferdinand, panicked, realizes that he will be the first to enter the stage. His growing anxiety overwhelms him and he begins to decompose, fearing to find himself alone in front of the audience. The other characters try to reassure him and motivate him, but Ferdinand's fear threatens to compromise the long-awaited spectacle. Through moments of camaraderie, hesitation and mutual support, this episode explores the themes of friendship, courage and perseverance, while promising unexpected twists and life lessons.

programme.title: The story of scalpel
programme.sub-title: Napoleon at St. Helena: the last act
programme.desc: "Napoleon at St.Hélène: the last act"In 1821, Napoleon Bonaparte died at the age of 51, after five years of exile on the island of St.Hélène. Philippe Charlier reopens this famous "cold case".
programme.desc-more: St. Helena was the last act of Napoleonic legend: the emperor lived there in exile, following his abdication after the defeat of Waterloo. He died there 5 years later, on May 5, 1821, at the age of 51. Excavations in his estate on the isolated British volcanic island in the South Atlantic reveal precarious living conditions. From the mortuary masks, Philippe Charlier tries to recreate the emperor's face, and the unfolding of his last days, allowing him to learn more about the circumstances of his death.

programme.title: Facing the story: Philippe Pétain's Ghost
programme.desc: "The myth of the savior"In June 1940, France collapsed and Marshal Pétain came to power. He took the tragic and shameful path of collaboration with the Nazis.
programme.desc-more: If Philippe Pétain had died in 1938, streets, schools and hospitals would bear his name. But in June 1940 France collapsed and Pétain came to power. The Marshal then took the tragic and shameful path of collaboration with the Nazis and set up the National Revolution which aims to exclude from the social body the "bad French". Today, Philippe Pétain's ghost still offers a mirror in which one can see the French fractures.

programme.title: Facing the story: Philippe Pétain's Ghost
programme.desc: "The Twilight of the Marshal" Sentenced to death, a sentence commuted to life imprisonment, Pétain died in 1951, at 95 years of age. How do the nostalgic of Pétain try to rehabilitate him?
programme.desc-more: After an exile at the castle of Sigmaringen in Germany, Pétain returned to France for his trial. After three weeks of heated debates, the Marshal was sentenced to death, a sentence commuted to life imprisonment. The bulky prisoner was imprisoned on the island of Yeu and died on July 23, 1951, at 95 years of age. How has his figure resurgently emerged in the political debate in recent decades? And in what way do the nostalgic of Pétain try to rehabilitate it, still today, using a dangerous revision of historical truths?

programme.title: Direct action, our years of lead
programme.desc: A review of the history and ideology of Direct Action, a terrorist group of far left who set France on fire and bloodshed between 1979 and 1987.
programme.desc-more: On 17 November 1986, the murder of businessman Georges Besse was one of the last acts committed by a terrorist group that has been spreading terror in France since 1979: Direct action. Between robberies, bomb attacks and assassinations, this extreme left group marked the French "years of lead". Today, there are more than 80 attacks by its members, with a total of 26 injured and 12 dead. Behind the history of this group are enlightened idealists who wanted to carry out their political action through the great banditry.

programme.title: Adventurers of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: In 1798, General Napoleon Bonaparte landed in Egypt with an army of soldiers, but also a contingent of scholars and artists. As the cannons roar, the Egyptian Institute was born in Cairo. Among the art and science men who took part in this extraordinary expedition, artist Dominique Vivant Denon was the first to travel the Nile at the risk of his life. From Cairo to Luxor, through Dendérah, he drew temples and colosses, fascinated by the greatness of the Pharaohs. While at Rosette, Bonaparte's troops discovered a stele engraved with three scriptures, which might well hold the key to the mystery of hieroglyphics.

programme.title: Adventurers of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: After the French defeat, Englishman William Richard Hamilton confiscates Rosette's stone and sends it to the British Museum. Napoleon had the "Description of Egypt", a monument of erudition that fascinated Europe, while in Cairo, the consul of France, Bernardino Drovetti, and the English consul Henry Salt, both hunters of ancient treasures, were fighting for the most beautiful pieces. A fight in which the Englishman will receive the help of a determined man: Giovanni Battista Belzoni. Salt and Belzoni want to send the "Memnon Youth" to London, a colossal bust that the French failed to take away. Drovetti is ready to do anything to stop them. In Egypt, the consul war is only beginning.

programme.title: Adventurers of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: The rivalry between the French and the English reached a high point. In Egypt, it's a wild race for treasures. The British took the advantage by attaching to the services of Italian Belzoni, who had succeeded in this. After reopening the temple of Abu Simbel in the south of the country, he was the first in thousands of years to enter the tomb of Sethi I, the father of Ramses II. Meanwhile, in Europe, the Frenchman Jean-François Champollion held the rope. Thanks to copies of Rosette's stone brought back by Bonaparte scientists, he managed to decipher the first hieroglyphs and took the advantage over his English competitor Thomas Young.

programme.title: Simon
programme.desc: Discover the summary of the episodes of season 2 of the Simons series
programme.desc-more: In a sunny environment where children's imagination reigns in master, Simon (Mathias Casartelli) is a young boy passionate about gliders. One day, as he devoted himself to his passion, he saw Ferdinand (Angèle Humeau), his comrade, making an incredible cardboard plane with wheels. Emerged by Ferdinand's creation, Simon eagerly wants to try it. Ferdinand, benevolent, accepts, but imposes a condition: Simon must first push him to test his invention. After several attempts, excitement turns into frustration when lunchtime arrives, and Simon has to leave the game. Back in the world, he discovered that Ferdinand once again wanted him to push him, which caused Simon to get angry and return to his glider, taking his brother with him. However, the happiness of the two brothers attracted Ferdinand, who, eager for camaraderie, sought to join them in their laughter and games. This quest for sharing and friendship illustrates the dynamics of childhood and the quest for inclusion.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: This funny and sincere look at modern family life celebrates how creative games help to shape children. Bluey, an Australian puppy-poy, has a mind-blowing imagination and loves to turn daily life into fun adventures. She and her little sister Bingo are embarking on exploring their world, using the game to overcome their fears and try to play adult roles. They are more pleased with nothing than to train their parents, especially their father, in their games. Mom, Chilli, went back to work, and Dad, Bandit, juggles between child care and telework. But if he thinks he's the one who commands it, it's the girls who lead the dance when it comes to playing, but also for everything else!
programme.desc-more: In a colorful and fun world, Bluey, a six-year-old Australian Bouvier puppy, lives thrilling adventures alongside her family. With an overly imagination, Bluey explores the world around her with insatiable curiosity. Each episode follows Bluey's games and interactions with her father, Bandit (David McCormack), and her mother, Chilli (Melanie Zanetti), who encourage her creative spirit while teaching her valuable life lessons. Whether it's transforming itself into a fearless explorer or organizing improvised shows, Bluey turns everyday situations into extraordinary adventures. The episodes also highlight relationships with her little sister, Bingo, and her friends, illustrating the challenges and joys of childhood. Through touching and humorous narratives, the series addresses universal themes such as friendship, family and imagination, captivating an audience of all ages.

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Peppa is a little mischievous and life-filled pig who shares her colorful universe with her little brother George, their mom Pig and their dad Pig. Together, they explore the world around them with curiosity and joy. Peppa loves to have fun, whether playing hide and seek, disguised as princesses or jumping in mud puddles, which gives him immense pleasure. Each episode highlights Peppa's and her family's daily adventures, while introducing a gallery of endearing characters, such as her friends Rebecca Rabbit and Suzy Mouton. Through simple situations and life lessons, Peppa learns essential values such as friendship, sharing and creativity. With its humor and good, contagious mood, Peppa invites young spectators to discover the world with a wonderful look, while cultivating their imagination.
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little slut full of life and energy, always ready to explore the world around her. programme.desc: Because reading is and will remain one of the best ways to escape, François Busnel invites viewers to enter "La P'tite Librairie". On shelves there are novels, essays, great classics or comic books. In short, books to eat without moderation to make the mind travel from its couch. François Busnel proposes every day to discover or rediscover a French or foreign work: novel, essay, great classic or comic strip. In short, this is a good opportunity to get to the page.

programme.title: Hot potato! Potato in danger
programme.desc: France is not only a major potato consumer, cooked in all its forms, but also the world's largest exporter. Focusing on the Hauts-de-France and Brittany, this potato culture brings with it its lot of problems. Indeed, its production requires a lot of energy and water and damages the soil. France therefore faces a huge challenge, namely to maintain its status as a potato master while taking into account the environmental and economic challenges associated with it.

programme.title: Madiba Challenge, a sporty, human and supportive adventure
programme.desc: The Madiba Challenge is the result of a meeting between the presenter Ismaël Khelifa and Siviwe Mbinda on a film of the show "Escaped Belle" in South Africa. The emerging friendship between the two men gave Ismaël the idea of launching this sporting challenge in tribute to Nelson Mandela, which must lead to the construction of a sports complex on site. Accompanied by his friend Théo Curin, a mandisport swimmer, they are followed by cameras during their physical and mental preparation for D-Day. At the key, 30 kilometers of relay swimming in Cape Town followed by 100 kilometers by bike to the township of Langa.

programme.title: Santorini and Milos, volcanic cycled

programme.title: Beautiful escapes
programme.desc: From the traditional "bouches" to the new Confluence district, the Lyon journalist shows local specialities. She went on a walk through the streets of Lyon with chef Grégory Cuilleron and the guide-concert Jean-Luc Chavent. Subjects: Lyon mothers or the art of perpetuating culinary traditions • In the course of the Saône, Confluence • The Paul Bocuse Institute: the art of exporting culinary know-how • The mysteries of Lyon • The wonders of the Golden Head Park • The Lyon balls.

These social, societal, environmental, climatic, economic or political issues are presented and analysed with a national or international prism.

programme.desc: Culture, politics, economy... In a Parisian loft, Anne-Elisabeth Lemoine and her group of columnists discuss and exchange around the most diverse news, live. The presenter is surrounded by Patrick Cohen, Pierre Lescure, Aurélie Casse alternately with Emilie Tran Nguyen, Mohamed Bouhafsi, Lorrain Sénéchal and Bertrand Chameroy. During the show, where they receive several guests, each presents a chronicle. programme.title: Thalassa, extreme adventures
programme.desc: Off the coast of Great Britain, the Scottish islands draw a world apart, between turquoise beaches, dizzying cliffs and the vast Atlantic. With the veterinarian and adventurer Cal Major, Diego approaches the large colonies of seabirds and discovers the fragile life that animates these isolated lands. On the island of Jura, three women made the bet to create their own gin, a unique adventure in the heart of wild landscapes. Then, on the coasts beaten by the winds, Diego faced the heights of the Old Man of Stoer, a granite tower erected above the waves. A sensitive and spectacular journey, to meet an unsumptuous nature and those who have chosen to live at its own pace.

programme.title: Thalassa, extreme adventures
programme.desc: In French Polynesia, in the heart of the Pacific Ocean, Diego Buñuel meets the apneist Denis Grosmaire with the aim of finding and observing a tiger shark. For several years, Denis Grosmaire has been accustomed to diving unprotected and spending time with sharks. It explains the potentially dangerous impact of a decline in shark numbers in the ocean. On the archipelago, Diego also meets a local biodiversity-conscious sinner and a photographer who takes pictures of surfers in action.

programme.title: C tonight
programme.desc: With French people more concerned than ever about the repercussions of the various political, health, social, economic, energy and war crises in Ukraine and the Middle East, intellectuals, artists and protagonists at the centre of the news come to bring their expertise to a debate. Karim Rissouli and Camille Diao, accompanied either by Laure Adler or Arthur Chevallier, receive several guests who provide answers to the questions that are topical while revealing their ideas. Ideas are the stars of this event, which highlights a diversity of views on the complexity of the world.

programme.title: Simon
programme.desc: Discover the summary of the episodes of season 2 of the Simons series
programme.desc-more: In a sunny environment where children's imagination reigns in master, Simon (Mathias Casartelli) is a young boy passionate about gliders. One day, as he devoted himself to his passion, he saw Ferdinand (Angèle Humeau), his comrade, making an incredible cardboard plane with wheels. Emerged by Ferdinand's creation, Simon eagerly wants to try it. Ferdinand, benevolent, accepts, but imposes a condition: Simon must first push him to test his invention. After several attempts, excitement turns into frustration when lunchtime arrives, and Simon has to leave the game. Back in the world, he discovered that Ferdinand once again wanted him to push him, which caused Simon to get angry and return to his glider, taking his brother with him. However, the happiness of the two brothers attracted Ferdinand, who, eager for camaraderie, sought to join them in their laughter and games. This quest for sharing and friendship illustrates the dynamics of childhood and the quest for inclusion.

Back in the world, he discovered that Ferdinand once again wanted him to push him, which caused Simon to get angry and return to his glider, taking his brother with him. However, the happiness of the two brothers attracted Ferdinand, who, eager for camaraderie, sought to join them in their laughter and games. This quest for sharing and friendship illustrates the dynamics of childhood and the quest for inclusion.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: This funny and sincere look at modern family life celebrates how creative games help to shape children. Bluey, an Australian puppy-poy, has a mind-blowing imagination and loves to turn daily life into fun adventures. She and her little sister Bingo are embarking on exploring their world, using the game to overcome their fears and try to play adult roles. They are more pleased with nothing than to train their parents, especially their father, in their games. Mom, Chilli, went back to work, and Dad, Bandit, juggles between child care and telework. But if he thinks he's the one who commands it, it's the girls who lead the dance when it comes to playing, but also for everything else!
programme.desc-more: In a colorful and fun world, Bluey, a six-year-old Australian Bouvier puppy, lives thrilling adventures alongside her family. With an overly imagination, Bluey explores the world around her with insatiable curiosity. Each episode follows Bluey's games and interactions with her father, Bandit (David McCormack), and her mother, Chilli (Melanie Zanetti), who encourage her creative spirit while teaching her valuable life lessons. Whether it's transforming itself into a fearless explorer or organizing improvised shows, Bluey turns everyday situations into extraordinary adventures. The episodes also highlight relationships with her little sister, Bingo, and her friends, illustrating the challenges and joys of childhood. Through touching and humorous narratives, the series addresses universal themes such as friendship, family and imagination, captivating an audience of all ages.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: In the colorful and sparkling world of Bluey, a young blue bitch, the daily adventure takes a playful and imaginative turn. Accompanied by her little sister Bingo, Bluey transforms everyday situations into captivating games. When Bluey receives an invitation to a birthday party, the excitement is at its peak. At the same time, their father, Bandit (David McCormack), is confronted with the challenges of daily life when he has to drive his daughters to school. The two little bitches, with their overly creativeness, will not fail to imagine hilarious and surprising scenarios, making each moment memorable. Through games that reflect their daily lives, Bluey and Bingo learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and imagination, while bringing joy and laughter to those around them.

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Peppa is a mischievous and dynamic pig girl who lives on rewarding adventures with her family, composed of her little brother George, her mom Pig and her dad Pig. In a colorful and fun world, Peppa and George explore their environment while learning to express their emotions and interact with others. Their days are punctuated with games in mud puddles, visits to friends like Suzy Sheep and Pedro Pony, and exciting discoveries, whether by painting, playing hide-and-seek or going to the farm. Through these moments of complicity, young spectators are invited to discover the values of friendship, family and curiosity. Awarded by a BAFTA Award in 2005 for its quality of pre-school animation, this exciting series offers an educational and entertaining universe for toddlers.
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little slut full of life and energy, always ready to explore the world around her. With his little brother George (Lily Snowden-Fine), they are living thrilling and fun adventures alongside their parents, Mom Pig and Papa Pig (Richard Ridings). Peppa loves jumping into mud puddles, an activity that gives him immense joy and symbolizes his mischievous spirit. Each episode takes them into a variety of situations, whether on a farm trip, a day at the beach, or even a simple visit to friends. Through these moments of play and discovery, Peppa and George learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and sharing. Colourful characters, such as their friend Suzy Sheep (Morwenna Banks) and the teacher, add a touch of magic to their daily lives, making each episode both educational and entertaining.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing is looking forward to using his new Hoppity sledge in the snow. But when he takes off his gloves to make a snowman, his hands hurt him.
programme.desc-more: In a world full of bright colours and joy, the Teletubes, small, joyful creatures with vibrant hues, spend their days exploring their peaceful landscape. Each one of them, with its unique personality, engages in fun and interactive activities, learning to discover and appreciate the world around them. Tinky Winky, the tallest, wears a mysterious pouch, while Dipsy, with his green hat, likes to dance and play. The sweet Laa-Laa, always accompanied by her ball, and the curious Po, the smallest of the group, add their touch of innocence to their adventures. Through games, laughter and moments of wonder, Teletubbies learn valuable lessons about friendship and sharing. Each episode is punctuated with the appearance of their ventral television screen, which broadcasts captivating videos of small children playing and having fun, thus reinforcing the idea that joy is found in daily interactions and discoveries.

programme.desc-more: In a colorful and fun world, Bluey's short films plunge us into the tender universe of Bluey and Bingo, two young puppies overflowing with imagination and curiosity. Each episode is a celebration of childhood, where the simple moments of daily life turn into hilarious and touching adventures. In this compilation, fans will find their favorite characters while discovering new memorable faces. Among them, Muffin, who starts in a video of unpacking, and the dad, who tries to get an unexpected tattoo, bring a touch of freshness and humour. The spectators will also have the opportunity to explore the backstage of Bluey's dream home and Bingo, a place where the imagination comes alive. Each short film highlights valuable life lessons, while celebrating brotherly love and family ties, in a setting where creativity and friendship are in the spotlight.

programme.title: The 100 places you need to see
programme.sub-title: The Pyrenees, land of history and transhumance
programme.desc: In the Pyrenees, from the Ossau valley to the Aspe valley, pastures of altitude are a wild territory intimately linked to transhumance, a secular practice.

programme.title: The bookstore
programme.desc: Because reading is and will remain one of the best ways to escape, François Busnel invites viewers to enter "La P'tite Librairie". On shelves there are novels, essays, great classics or comic books. In short, books to eat without moderation to make the mind travel from its couch. François Busnel proposes every day to discover or rediscover a French or foreign work: novel, essay, great classic or comic strip. In short, this is a good opportunity to get to the page.

programme.title: The Treasures of Shu's Kingdom
programme.desc: A team of archaeologists, historians and scientists have uncovered a city that has been forgotten for millennia in southwestern China. They try to lift the veil on this great civilization until then unknown, upsetting the history of antiquity. Thousands of objects, bronze, jade and gold relics, dating back more than three thousand years, are back in the light. The site is a testimony to a sophisticated civilization with advanced metallurgy, complex urban planning and a rich belief system centered on the cult of the sun. The history of this fascinating international scientific inquiry offers a renewed reading of the origins of ancient China.

programme.title: Winning return for the kitchen of old
programme.desc: Once put in the old grimoires, the recipes of old make a frantic return today on social networks, in bookstores and in starred restaurants. This phenomenon, which combines nostalgia, a quest for meaning, conviviality and eco-responsible approach, demonstrates a deep need to reconnect with our roots but also with "good eating". Constance has made her 86-year-old Mamou a social media star by filming her preparing her family recipes. Some restaurateurs, like Jean Sévénes, surf on their childhood memories. Elsewhere, others do not hesitate to rehabilitate the offal or to put the soup in fashion.

programme.title: The 100 places you need to see
programme.sub-title: The path of customs officers, from Mont-Saint-Michel to Quiberon

programme.title: Beautiful escapes

programme.title: Here. The most beautiful years of our life
programme.desc: In New Jersey, a majestic early 20th-century house stands proudly on a historic land, once inhabited by dinosaurs and once owned by Benjamin Franklin's family. This home becomes the scene of existences rich in emotions, where an aviator (Tom Hanks) and his wife, an inventor and his companion meet, as well as an elegant dancer, each carrying ambitious dreams and personal challenges to overcome. At the centre of this saga is Al (Paul Bettany), a veteran of the Second World War, and his wife Rose (Kelly Reilly), who are looking forward to the arrival of their first child, Richard. The years went by, and Richard, who had grown up, managed to introduce Margaret (Michelle Dockery) to her parents, marking the dawn of a new generation. As Margaret prepares to become Richard's companion and their little daughter's mother, Vanessa, the house bears witness to the joys and sorrows of a deeply human life.

programme.desc: Following the 1986 coup d'état, the northern Uganda was shaken by the violence committed by the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA). programme.desc: In Nuremberg in the 16th century, the executioner's profession was passed on from father to son. With humility, Frantz Schmidt does his daily work, which demeans him as a farmman or as a defiler. As part of the Holy Roman Empire, Nuremberg was a thriving, economic and cultural city. But several epidemics and bad harvests, followed by famine and inflation, lead to economic stagnation and an increase in crime. Morally exemplary, Frantz Schmidt will take advantage of this context to wash the honor of his family, and raise it to the higher social rank.

programme.title: Homo Animalis, a strange species
programme.desc: Among the 7 million or so animal species that inhabit the planet, one of them has its uniqueity: Homo sapiens. But while its senses are limited, compared to those of other animals, how can we explain that this biped with the gripping thumb has spread over the entire earth's surface? In immersion in a campsite - the man willingly letting appear his true nature during the migration of summer holidays -, two naturalists quinquennials will observe a group of individuals to highlight typical behaviors of the species: learning faculties and thirst for knowledge, physical activities, taste for play, social interactions, rituals of seduction.

programme.title: Meuh! The horns' epic
programme.desc: It was in Anatolia, in eastern Turkey, that the ancestor common to all the bovids, the aurochs, began to be domesticated ten thousand years ago. Today, on the high plateaus, Turkish villagers perpetuate the multi-year tradition of transhumance and estiva, as close as possible to their herds. In Portugal, beef remains used for ploughing terraced plots.

programme.title: Meuh! The horns' epic
programme.sub-title: The Zebu to conquer the arid
programme.desc: A domesticated form of Indian aurochs, zebu is particularly suitable for dry, even desert climates, where water and food may sometimes be lacking for weeks. In a few millennia he has travelled from the Indus to the gates of Europe and the borders of Africa, where he is still raised in flocks.

programme.title: Meuh! The horns' epic
programme.desc: South Asian wetlands and forests emerged from the water buffalo, a natural force adapted to marshy areas. He was domesticated and first allowed men to cultivate these lands and in some areas became a spiritual figure. In Brazil, it has naturally been part of the Amazon River estuary. Yet, the buffalo has been gradually abandoned in the field work.

programme.title: Meuh! The horns' epic

programme.desc: A symbol of the Tibet plateau and Himalayas, the Yak has been able to map trade routes thanks to its resistance to extreme temperatures and endurance.

programme.title: The Count of Monte Cristo: Treason
programme.desc: In 1815 Edmond Dantès (Jean Marais), a promising young sailor, took command of the ship Pharaoh after the death of his captain. While he stopped at the island of Elbe to deliver a message to Napoleon, his return to Marseilles was marked by intense joy, as he was about to marry his beloved, Mercedes (Lia Amanda). However, the jealousy of Fernand (Roger Pigaut), Mercedes' cousin, and the machinations of other conspirators, who see him as a threat to their ambitions, lead to his betrayal. Accused of Bonapartism, Dantès was imprisoned at the sinister castle of If, where he endured years of suffering. In this isolation, he discovered a plan of escape and met a former prisoner, Abbé Faria, who transmitted him with valuable knowledge. Once free, Dantès turned into a Count of Monte Cristo, determined to orchestrate a relentless revenge against those who destroyed his life.

programme.title: The Count of Monte Cristo: Revenge
programme.desc: Dantes, now known as Count de Monte-Cristo, returns to Paris with one goal in mind: revenge. He was supported by his faithful companion Jacopo, and immerse himself in the Parisian world where he discovered that his former rival, Fernand (Roger Pigaut), had become General Count of Morcerf and Mercedes's husband (Lia Amanda), his former love. By saving Fernand from a rixe, Dantès crossed the path of Albert (Jean Marais), the son of Mercedes, who did not doubt the true identity of his savior. Although Mercedes recognizes her former fiancé as Dantes, she is torn between her past and her present, refusing to flee with him. As Dantès weaves his web of revenge, he must navigate a world of betrayal, secrets and confrontations that will test his convictions and his desire for justice.

programme.title: Water keepers
programme.desc: In Nagaland, a northeastern state of India, the inhabitants store monsoon water in rain ponds. These reservoirs allow the land to be irrigated during the dry season at the cost of permanent maintenance.

programme.title: The Count of Monte Cristo: Treason
programme.desc: A man who was the victim of a slanderous denunciation was thrown into prison where he was in prison for 18 long years before seeking revenge for this injustice.
programme.desc-more: In 1815 Edmond Dantès (Jean Marais), a promising young sailor, took command of the ship Pharaoh after the death of his captain. While he stopped at the island of Elbe to deliver a message to Napoleon, his return to Marseilles was marked by intense joy, as he was about to marry his beloved, Mercedes (Lia Amanda). However, the jealousy of Fernand (Roger Pigaut), Mercedes' cousin, and the machinations of other conspirators, who see him as a threat to their ambitions, lead to his betrayal. Accused of Bonapartism, Dantès was imprisoned at the sinister castle of If, where he endured years of suffering. In this isolation, he discovered a plan of escape and met a former prisoner, Abbé Faria, who transmitted him with valuable knowledge. Once free, Dantès turned into a Count of Monte Cristo, determined to orchestrate a relentless revenge against those who destroyed his life.

programme.title: The Count of Monte Cristo: Revenge

programme.desc-more: Dantes, now known as Count de Monte-Cristo, returns to Paris with one goal in mind: revenge. He was supported by his faithful companion Jacopo, and immerse himself in the Parisian world where he discovered that his former rival, Fernand (Roger Pigaut), had become General Count of Morcerf and Mercedes's husband (Lia Amanda), his former love. By saving Fernand from a rixe, Dantès crossed the path of Albert (Jean Marais), the son of Mercedes, who did not doubt the true identity of his savior. Although Mercedes recognizes her former fiancé as Dantes, she is torn between her past and her present, refusing to flee with him. As Dantès weaves his web of revenge, he must navigate a world of betrayal, secrets and confrontations that will test his convictions and his desire for justice.

programme.title: When females have power: the matriarchate in the animal world
programme.desc: In northwestern Namibia, Damara's mole rats evolve within a colony governed by a queen, much more powerful than its subjects.
programme.desc-more: Elephants are not the only matriarchal animal society: some communities of hyenas, makis, mole rats or suricates are also regulated by females. From Namibia to Madagascar and Tanzania, this planetary round-up challenges the dominant male theorem. These lifestyles, which have been studied more closely by teams of researchers in recent years, reveal other strategies, such as ritualized submission rather than oppression or aggressiveness.

programme.title: Collective Parenthood, a key to evolution
programme.desc: What role has the ability to collectively care for the youngest people played in the evolution of the human species? Update on the latest advances in research.
programme.desc-more: For scientists, human prosocial behaviour – the ability we have to care for others in a disinterested way, and especially through motherhood – could be a key to understanding our evolution. After its birth, a small human is much less self-sufficient than a newborn from other species. He needs a long period of maturation, and needs attention and stimulation that a single person, his mother in the first place, can hardly give him. Archaeological research on funeral practices in the Bronze and Iron Ages revealed the social role of women other than their biological mothers in young children.

programme.title: The waltz of continents
programme.desc: Built by three gigantic collisions with America, Asia and Africa, the European continent is constantly evolving, as the imminent earthquakes show.
programme.desc-more: In five episodes, an analysis of how the five continents were born, grew and disappeared. This first part is dedicated to the origins of the Old Continent. Europe has been built by three gigantic collisions with the future America, Asia and Africa. Each has caused cataclysms of a prodigious magnitude that have created a world of chaotic forms and bright colors. Over time, mountain ranges higher than Himalayas have been established in Scandinavia and Scotland, where the great plains of the centre are now found. After millions of years of erosion, Europe has become a sea bottom, invaded by unusual forms of life that have sometimes even changed its shape.

programme.title: Dracula: the true story
programme.desc: In the 15th century, Romanian prince Vlad Tepes terrified his enemies by his cruel empalations, inspiring much later the famous myth of Dracula.
programme.desc-more: Born under the pen of the Irish writer Bram Stoker, Dracula has haunted imaginations for more than a century. But behind the myth lies a Romanian prince who shook Europe in his time: Vlad III, prince of Valachie, also known in his time as Vlad Tepes. Thanks to the recent invention of the printing press, the more or less amplified narratives of its crimes spread to the west of the continent, where they serve as a support for a new imagination that will last for centuries. Together with researchers, this documentary, illustrated with red scenes made in rotoscopy, iconographic representations and animated maps, is part of the traces of the real Dracula.

programme.title: Artificial Intelligence: The ultimate human invention?
programme.desc: Artificial intelligence is progressing at a dizzying speed, generating as much enthusiasm as anxiety. How can we keep control of this technology?
programme.desc-more: For a long time, considered a promising yet still infancy technology, artificial intelligence is now evolving at a dizzying pace. From the first networks of neurons to increasingly autonomous systems, this documentary traces decades of research by combining archives and testimonies of pioneer researchers. A multi-voice story that makes the history of a technological revolution intersect with the questions it raises today.

He compares his views with those of former employees of large AI companies, those working for his safety and families directly confronted with the drifts of certain chatbots. A multi-voice story that makes the history of a technological revolution intersect with the questions it raises today.

programme.desc: Two modest bank employees in Buenos Aires are embarking on an unlikely run after stealing a large amount of money from their institution.
programme.desc-more: Morán, employed in the branch of a bank in Buenos Aires, makes numerous round trips to the safes of the establishment during his working days and is forced to manipulate large sums of cash. One evening, after work, with a bag, he went to a bar where he invited Román, one of his colleagues, to whom he made an important revelation: he stole a large sum of money from the bank that employs them, wanted to entrust him with this loot and then go to the police. Once his prison sentence has been served, Morán and Román are supposed to meet again to share this money, which must allow them to stop working for the rest of their lives.

programme.title: Ireland, between land and sea
programme.desc: Ireland is full of amazing landscapes, between green pastures, peatlands and crystal clear waters. A historical and visual journey to the heart of a country with austere beauty.
programme.desc-more: Between green pastures, peatlands and crystal clear waters, Ireland is full of splendid panoramas, rough beauty. This documentary takes a look at the different environments of "the island of emerald". In Malin Head, the dizzying cliffs dominate the Atlantic Ocean. The Connemara wilderness contains remains from 6,000 to 10,000 years old. In the southeast of the island, Bannow Bay is a Viking heritage. Finally, the very wild Beara Peninsula has a stunning Atlantic forest, which is being rebuilt.

programme.title: Irish islands, ocean outposts
programme.desc: Winter storms to summer mist: on the wild islands of northwestern Ireland, animals must survive the intense rhythm of the seasons.
programme.desc-more: The northwestern part of Ireland is dotted with wild islands where nature reigns as the mistress. Away from the rest of the world, the archipelago is home to an impressive diversity of wildlife: while birds nest on Toraigh Island and grey seals fight for supremacy on the Inishkea Islands, humpback whales are killed off the Blasket Archipelago. Under harsh climatic conditions, these species must adapt their survival strategies over the seasons.

programme.title: Irish islands, ocean outposts
programme.desc: The arrival of spring leaves room for a wet and cottony fog. Many species of animals must constantly adapt to survive.
programme.desc-more: On the islands of northwestern Ireland, time seems to have stopped: far from the tumult of cities, the bright greenery of pastures invariably melts in the blue of the ocean. Yet the seasons follow each other and are not the same. As the elements unfold in winter, the arrival of spring leaves room for a wet and cottony fog. Therefore, the many species of animals present on the archipelago must constantly adapt to survive. When summer settles, nearly 250,000 seabirds migrate to Rathlin Island to nest on tree-lined cliffs. In autumn, off the Aran Islands, hundreds of pilgrim sharks gather: swimming in concentric circles, they are here engaged in an amazing speed dating.

programme.title: Slavery and its networks: The weight of colonial heritage
programme.desc: The Atlantic trade has undoubtedly enriched Europe. In tracing the financial flows of slavery, the debate on reparations is being questioned.
programme.desc-more: Between the 16th and 19th centuries, millions of Africans were enslaved and deported to the Americas to work in sugar, cotton and tobacco plantations. The Atlantic trade irrigates the European economy far beyond the ports concerned. If it contributes to the development of cities such as Liverpool, Bordeaux or Amsterdam, its benefits extend to the territories of the Holy Roman Empire, where merchants, investors and plantation owners take part in this system. Long unknown, the origin of many fortunes built on slavery is now gradually discovered by research.

programme.title: The tragic story of Fritz the elephant
programme.desc: At the edge of the 20th century, hundreds of thousands of wild animals from Africa and Asia are captured each year, destined for circuses and museums. The major European cities - Paris, London, Antwerp, Berlin... - then pride themselves on zoological gardens, to satisfy the desires of the public. Captured in India, Fritz the elephant was then exploited in the famous American circus Barnum. In 1902, he revolted in the middle of the street... Today he sits behind a window of the Museum of Fine Arts of Tours.

programme.title: Russian lawyers in Moscow's sight
programme.desc: Fake trials, illegal arrests, repression of independent lawyers: in Russia, since Putin's arrival in power, the judicial system is now only the shadow of itself. However, some legal professionals continue to fight for justice: under absurd accusations, Mikhail Benyash has been standing up to the state's judiciary for several years. In 2022, he publicly denounced the invasion of Ukraine and defended soldiers who had refused to leave the front. His famous colleague Karinna Moskalkenko also challenges the Kremlin, this time from the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg.

programme.title: The iron curtain of Czechoslovakia
programme.desc: Three decades after the collapse of the USSR, the Czech Republic is looking at those who died on the borders with Germany and Austria trying to escape the communist regime. After the case was filed by the NGO Platform of European Memory and Consciousness, which brought the cases before the Prague and Weiden courts in Germany, forty-one persons are now under investigation. Among them, three former members of the Politburo of the time. Benefiting from the valuable experience of the German authorities who worked on the deaths of the Berlin Wall, the Czech Republic is thus beginning a long process of memory and justice, which should help the families of the victims to heal their wounds, and the whole country to better understand its past.

programme.title: The Little Wadrouille
programme.desc: After a professional conference, Franck (Daniel Auteuil), a businessman with romantic ambitions, asked his right-hand man Justine (Sandrine Kiberlain) to organize a special weekend with a woman he barely knew. By giving him a generous sum of money and complete freedom for the preparations, he leaves him to make this getaway unforgettable. Justine, excited by this mission, immediately talks to her companion Albin (Denis Podalydes). The latter, an opportunist, sees it as a chance to earn a little money easily and to improve the lives of their eccentric group of friends. However, an unexpected turnaround is on the horizon: the woman Franck imagines for this weekend is none other than Justine herself. As projects take on a comical and unpredictable turn, Justine must juggle her feelings, professional expectations and the quiproquos that are constantly accumulating. The plot is complicated as Albin, aware of the situation, tries to intervene, transforming this romantic weekend into a veritable whirlwind of adventures and revelations.

programme.title: The double lover
programme.desc: Chloe Fortin, a model, has long been a victim of stomach aches that she cannot explain. His gynaecologist then directed him to Paul Meyer, a psychotherapist. From the second session, the young woman tells the therapist a very intimate dream. The sessions, often filled with painful memories, follow for months, during which Chloe tells his difficult journey to the silent patriarch. When this one ends up talking, something is released for the patient who finally finds the smile. She also realizes that she is strongly attached to Paul.

programme.title: The Marquis de Sade or Justine's woes
programme.desc: Justine or the misfortunes of virtue: since its first publication in 1791, the sulfurous novel of the Marquis de Sade has never ceased to arouse repulsion and fascination. History of a scandal that resists time, mirroring history and the evolution of mentalities.

programme.title: Slumdog Millionaire
programme.desc: Jamal Malik (Dev Patel), an 18-year-old from the slums of Bombay, is on the stage of the famous TV game "Who wants to make millions?", where he is to an answer to get the much-loved jackpot. However, his fulcruming ascent attracts the attention of Prem Kumar (Anil Kapoor), the programme's facilitator, who suspects Jamal of cheating because of his difficult past. Jamal was imprisoned and subjected to a police detective's strong interrogation, and he was not allowed to be shot. He began to tell his tumultuous story, marked by the tragedy of his mother's loss, murdered by Hindu extremists. Together with his brother Salim (Raj Zutshi), they are forced to survive in a ruthless world, where they meet Latika (Freida Pinto), a young girl who will change the course of her life. Between love, betrayal and survival, Jamal reveals how every issue of the game is linked to its chaotic journey, revealing the trials that shaped it and the hope that drives it to fight for a better future.

programme.title: My different child
programme.desc: The life of Eva (Liv Lisa Fries), a devoted mother, is deeply affected by the unpredictable behaviour of her son Felix (Jona Eisenblätter), who has Asperger's syndrome. Felix's anger attacks and unexpected fugues put a severe strain on the balance of their daily lives and complicate his integration into college. To help him, an educational assistant is assigned to Felix, but the challenges remain. The situation becomes critical when Eva's employer is considering dismissing her because of her repeated absences from work related to her son's problems. In the face of this threat, Eva turns to her friend Martin for support. At the same time, Felix developed a surprising friendship with their next-door neighbor, a fisherman (Thure Lindhardt), who taught him the subtleties of his profession. The study of its cells, still cultivated in the laboratory, marked a turning point in medicine. Thanks to new microscopy techniques, science can now act on proteins, molecular motors and mitochondria, which produce energy and coordinate vital functions. From former footballer Sergi Samper's type 1 diabetes to the exceptional intervention on a girl's heart, cell research transforms our understanding of diseases and brings new therapies to life.

programme.sub-title: At the source of vital energy

Some molecules could slow down cell degradation and prolong life. The story of Towana Looney, one of the first patients to receive a genetically modified pig kidney, illustrates the promise and risks of these new approaches. Researchers are also trying to save the white northern rhinoceros by creating germ cells from their skin. Progress that raises an essential question: how far can we get on the living?

programme.title: The glass blower
programme.desc: In the heart of late 19th century imperial Germany, the Glass Breather plunges into the fascinating and ruthless universe of Thuringian glassmaking workshops, where the artisanal tradition is confronted with the upheavals of a changing era. Between the burning furnaces and the snow-covered forests, this historical drama depicts the fate of two sisters united by blood, but divided by choices that will lead them to the limits of their convictions and resilience. Johanna Steinmann, the elder, embodies the quiet force and sense of sacrifice. After the brutal disappearance of their father, a respected glass master, she alone assumed the burden of family survival. She left the ancestral home without hesitation to become an assistant to Mr. Strobel, a discreet and unscrupulous merchant whose commercial methods contrasted with Steinmann's artisanal heritage. In this urban world where ambition and cold transactions reign, Johanna discovers a ruthless reality, but also an independence she had never dared to imagine. For her part, Marie Steinmann, the youngest, inherits the talent and passion of their father for the work of glass. His gift for this delicate art attracts the attention of Wilhelm Heimer, an influential and respected glassmaker, who sees in her a protected person able to perpetuate her heritage. Under her wing, Mary shears, but quickly comes up against the limits imposed by a society that considers women to be wives and mothers first and foremost. Pushed by her family and by the conventions, she plans to marry Wilhelm's son, a marriage that would provide her with material security, but at the cost of her creative freedom. Distiled between her artistic ambition and her expectations, Mary feels trapped in a destiny she has not chosen.

More than a thousand years ago, from the Pyrenees to the North Sea, this mythical sovereign managed to rule over a large part of Europe from 768 until his death in 814. From his capital of Aachen, this conqueror, crowned emperor by the pope in the year 800, shaped a kingdom then without equivalent, organized and centralized: multi-educated schools, a structured administration, a strengthened clergy and even a single currency. What to call Charlemagne, the "father of Europe" and make him, after his death, a Christian saint.

programme.desc: In the Drôme, Marco Forconi manages with his associates a farm where the breeding is integrated into the ecosystem's balances. In the face of the intensification of droughts, he found in his quest for water an unexpected ally: beavers. Set up along the stream that crosses its land, they turned previously grilled meadows into green pastures. For these creatures, half-aquatic, half-terrestrial, build dams that slow down the flow of water and create wetlands, promoting soil rehydration and ecosystem regeneration. But while rodents have deserted their farm for a year, Marco decides to go on the beaver trail to learn more about his history, lifestyle and ecological role.

His underground workshop, transformed into a real bastion of freedom, became the scene of his heroic commitment. Animated archives and sequences inspired by ink drawing - a visual tribute to the tool that was his best weapon -, reveal the legacy of an extraordinary man and the journey of a craftsman of courage who marked the great causes of the twentieth century.

programme.title: France - Cambodia, so far, so close
programme.desc: How did Cambodia, marked by genocide, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? Back to historical links between Phnom Penh and Paris.
programme.desc-more: How did Cambodia, ravaged less than fifty years ago by one of the most deadly genocides of the twentieth century, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? And what remains, more than 160 years after the protectorate chosen by King Norodom I in 1863, of the singular bond between Phnom Penh and Paris? The common history of the two countries is that of a passionate relationship: a protectorate requested rather than impossibly, an independence obtained without confrontation by Norodom Sihanouk in 1953, and then the collapse under Pol Pot's regime. Peace is negotiated in Paris at the 1991 Conference. Those who have lived it from the inside tell behind the scenes. Cambodian officials are talking about reconstruction, the delicate balance between China, Vietnam and the West, and the place France can still hold.

programme.title: Pier 8
programme.desc: Former Member of Parliament for the English Channel, Minister of the Interior and then Prime Minister of François Hollande, Bernard Cazereu called for a "coalition of the hires " to re-establish France. It advocates stronger parliamentary power, greater citizen involvement and faster law-making to respond to the emergencies of our time.

programme.title: The Art of Losing in Politics
programme.desc: Failure reveals politicians much more than victory: former Presidents, Prime Ministers and MPs are unfailingly engaged in defeat.
programme.desc-more: From Nicolas Sarkozy to Valérie Pécresse, from François Hollande to Manuel Valls, Jean-François Copé, and Agnès Buzyn and Laurence Rossignol, they agreed for the first time to tell the story of the moments when their destiny is changing. And the next few days: friends who run away, the phone that no longer rings, the desire to disappear. After the night of defeat shock come the days after then the lessons. Some will throw the sponge, others will go through a depression or turn their failure into a future victory. With a unique display-mirror device in which the political personality interviewed looks at the evening images of his defeat, then finds himself facing himself and his reflection, and thanks to the archives of the INA, this documentary raises the veil on a taboo of political life.

programme.title: The Luron in the countryside
programme.desc: Humorist, imitator, singer, the well-named Thierry Le Luron was for about ten years the most caustic satirist in French political life.
programme.desc-more: Thierry Le Luron is one of the most provocative comedians of his time. In sketch, song or imitation, the satirist took a clever pleasure in caricatures without complacency the political figures of all sides of the era, from François Mitterrand to Raymond Barre, Georges Marchais and Jacques Chirac, and the 1981 presidential election was a playground for its projections. If some accepted his satires, others took him much more harm and sent him the tax.

programme.title: Adolfo Kaminsky, the free forger
programme.desc: From its first forgeries to protect Jewish children threatened by deportation to its central role in the clandestine struggles for freedom through the Resistance and anti-colonial fighting, Adolfo Kaminsky embodies an intimate and fierce fight against injustice in all its forms. His underground workshop, transformed into a real bastion of freedom, became the scene of his heroic commitment. Animated archives and sequences inspired by ink drawing - a visual tribute to the tool that was his best weapon -, reveal the legacy of an extraordinary man and the journey of a craftsman of courage who marked the great causes of the twentieth century.

programme.title: Heritage of France
programme.desc: In the Middle Ages, Champagne was at the centre of trade. Saint-Malo owes his reputation to important families of Breton merchants and shipowners.
programme.desc-more: Champagne, the invention of the medieval supermarket. While Champagne was always a region of passage, in the Middle Ages it was at the center of trade with its famous fairs. Thanks to the genius of the Counts of Champagne who managed to organize and secure these well-known markets, the territory has been permanently modified. Roads, built bridges but also entire cities like Provins have been created. - Saint-Malo, the genius of business and the sea. A proud citadel with imposing bourgeois houses and walls of stunning enclosures stands at the tip of the Ille-et-Vilaine. Saint-Malo owes his reputation and stature to important families of Breton merchants and shipowners.

programme.title: Tomorrow Havana
programme.desc: Five young Cubans have agreed to tell their daily lives in Havana and paint a picture of an island that is breathless, where everyone struggles in their own way to get out of it.
programme.desc-more: Asphyxiated by the embargo and paralyzed by an authoritarian and centralized system that struggles to reform, Cuba is going through one of the worst crises in its history. For the first time, five young Cubans agreed to tell their stories and to unveil their daily lives in Havana. In these exceptional stories and life slices, between the ruined buildings, the garbage that piles up, the water and electricity cuts, the endless lines in front of the shops and the constant surveillance of the State Security, is portrayed as an island with breathless breath where each struggles in his own way to get out of it.

programme.title: The man who defied Beijing
programme.desc: Liu Xiaobo, figure of the Tian'anmen uprising, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2010. Imprisoned and died in 2017, his destiny questions the history of China.
programme.desc-more: In the spring of 1989, when the students occupied Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, Liu Xiaobo, a Chinese literature researcher and outstanding speaker, became one of the movement's mentors. Arrested on 6 June, he was sent to the rehabilitation camp. Upon his release, a year and a half later, he chose to remain in China and resist from the inside. Arrested in 2008, he was sentenced to 11 years in prison. Still incarcerated in 2010, he cannot receive the Nobel Peace Prize in person and dies in captivity in July 2017. Today, the Chinese regime is making every effort to make Liu Xiaobo's name forgotten. But in 2008, the dissident entrusted his will in the form of a long interview. It is used as a frame by Pierre Haski to paint a portrait of a man who, throughout his life, fought for his convictions.

programme.title: Polisse
programme.desc: The daily, not always easy, of agents of the Brigade de protection des mineurs de Paris, who lead with private life and professional life.
programme.desc-more: Dive into the brutal effervescence and tearing daily life of the Brigade de Protection des Mineurs in Paris, Polisse unmistakably portrays the fierce fight of police officers facing the worst realities of the flouted childhood. Between the walls of a police station where the loudspeakers of voices and the heavy silences of unsaid people echo, these men and women – Fred (JoeyStarr), impulsive but deeply human, Nadine (Karin Viard), torn between his professional life and his sentimental failures, or Iris (Marina Foïs), whose fragility is hidden under a carapace of professionalism – trying to protect the most vulnerable. Incests, domestic violence, sordid trafficking, forced marriages: every case that lands on their desk is an open wound, a race against the clock to save lives that are already too marked. In the midst of this chaos, Mélissa (Maïwenn), a photographer in search of meaning, is immigrating into their universe for a report. Her external, first clinical, look is rapidly disturbed by the intensity of the drama she discovers, but also by the solidarity and brutal humanity of these cops used by their profession. An attitude arises between her and Fred, as fulcruming as it is improbable, while the brigade's internal tensions explode: nervous laughter to decompress, fierce strife, and this silent anorexia that gnaws Iris, reflecting the exhaustion of an entire team.

programme.title: Heritage of France
programme.desc: Between the city of Gerande and the peninsula of the Croisic stretch out the largest northern salt marshes of Europe. In Franche-Comté, pastures are full of salt.
programme.desc-more: Gerande, a fortune born of salt. In the extreme south of Brittany the largest northern salt marshes of Europe are spread. Between the medieval city of Guérande and the peninsula of the Croisic, the curves and geometric shapes of these salt marshes tell a history of more than a thousand years. - The salty destiny of the Franche-Comté. On the reliefs of Franche-Comté, the woods and pastures spread as far as possible and conceal a hidden treasure, salt. From the Middle Ages, men began to exploit the salt springs flowing into the Frankish-Comtine basements. Over the centuries, this manna has transformed the economy and face of this region of eastern France, as evidenced by the impressive Royal Saline of Arc-et-Senans, the jewel of 18th-century architecture.

The text, which was co-signed by the Member of Parliament Constance de Pélichy, was co-signed by deputies from 9 parliamentary groups. "DPI-A" is a diagnosis that detects chromosomal abnormalities in the embryo. Unauthorised in France, except in rare cases, this examination is allowed in Belgium and Spain. Find the beginning of the examination of the text in committee.

programme.title: The latest reel, Pierre Schoendoerffer and lost images of Diên Bien Phu
programme.desc: In May 1954, at Diên Bien Phu, in Indochina, Pierre Schoendoerffer filmed the battle and then had to abandon his films. Photographer Thomas Goisque tries to find them.
programme.desc-more: On 7 May 1954, the fall of the cut-off camp of Diên Biên Phu sealed the end of the Indochina war and precipitated the end of the French colonial Empire. From the ultimate assault, there is almost no French image left. At the heart of the battle, a young cameraman from the army, Pierre Schoendoerffer, filmed the war as closely as possible. He is taken prisoner and must abandon his equipment and film. But have all of his images really disappeared? Would they have left Vietnam after his capture? Would they have been taken to the Soviet Union? At the end of his life, Pierre Schoendoerffer still felt sorry for never having found these images. A war photographer, friend and spiritual heir of the filmmaker, Thomas Goisque has been gathering the clues left behind for several years.

programme.title: Primary, a machine to lose?
programme.desc: In two decades, primary schools have changed French political life. Presented as a democratic progress designed to give the activists the floor and legitimize the candidates, they nevertheless produced a spectacular paradox: in 2017, their two winners, François Fillon and Benoît Hamon, were swept away from the first round of the presidential election, opening the way for Emmanuel Macron and causing the long-term collapse of the traditional parties. Through a haunting chronological narrative, fed by the INA archives of the major television debates and exclusive testimonies of key actors - favorites, outsiders, small candidates and sounders - The documentary tells this modern political tragedy, where each election acts as a revealing of internal fractures and questions a system that struggles to gather.

programme.title: Chemical submission: for shame to change sides
programme.desc: On 19 December 2024, the verdict of the so-called Mazan rape trial was handed down, with 46 convictions. The victim, Gisèle Pelicot, was subjected to chemical submission by her own husband, a notion that was not known to the public until then. This case has helped to lift the veil on an abhorrent practice. Caroline Darian, the victim's daughter, goes back to the trial but also to many other women, who have suffered sexual violence, such as Zoé, Céline, Léa and Katia.

programme.title: Tomorrow Havana
programme.desc: Asphyxiated by the embargo and paralyzed by an authoritarian and centralized system that struggles to reform, Cuba is going through one of the worst crises in its history. For the first time, five young Cubans agreed to tell their stories and to unveil their daily lives in Havana. In these exceptional stories and life slices, between the ruined buildings, the garbage that piles up, the water and electricity cuts, the endless lines in front of the shops and the constant surveillance of the State Security, is portrayed as an island with breathless breath where each struggles in his own way to get out of it.

programme.title: Enrico Mattei, the oil rebel
programme.desc: On 27 October 1962, Enrico Mattei's plane crashed. Then disappeared "the most powerful Italian since Julius Caesar", founder of the ENI, the Italian oil company, the man who dared to challenge the Anglo-American cartel of the Seven Sisters. The word "sabotage" then circulates throughout Italy, but an expeditious investigation imposes the thesis of the accident. In a dark film atmosphere, the film traces the fulcruming rise of this franc-tireur, which supports the independences of colonized countries, whose daring upset the geopolitical balances of the Cold War.

programme.title: France - Cambodia, so far, so close
programme.desc: How did Cambodia, ravaged less than fifty years ago by one of the most deadly genocides of the twentieth century, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? And what remains, more than 160 years after the protectorate chosen by King Norodom I in 1863, of the singular bond between Phnom Penh and Paris? The common history of the two countries is that of a passionate relationship: a protectorate requested rather than impossibly, an independence obtained without confrontation by Norodom Sihanouk in 1953, and then the collapse under Pol Pot's regime. Peace is negotiated in Paris at the 1991 Conference. Those who have lived it from the inside tell behind the scenes. Cambodian officials are talking about reconstruction, the delicate balance between China, Vietnam and the West, and the place France can still hold.

Questions staggered, true/false, quotes from more or less exact leaders, interro by Philippe Aghion, the Nobel Prize in Economics: students, supported by business leaders, will play, confront each other, be wrong, learn and debate. Objective: to understand the economy by having fun! For this season 2, we find the main events of the show: "Do not have to have done the ENA", "the Deconometer", "You have the average?", "A True Un False?" and "The Nobel Prize Interro".

programme.title: In my city
programme.desc: Like many French cities, Clermont-Ferrand faces a wave of violence of unprecedented magnitude due to the explosion of drug trafficking.

programme.title: In my city
programme.desc: Many French cities are facing overtourism. Close-up on Chamonix, capital of mountaineering, very busy summer and winter.

programme.title: Mediterranean
programme.desc: A meeting dedicated to the Mediterranean world: history, cultures, societies and contemporary issues, through surveys and reports in various countries of the basin.

programme.title: Gabin, a peasant soul
programme.desc: Jean Gabin, a legendary actor, had a dream of settling in the countryside, far from the tumult of cinema. In Normandy, he found a property where he hoped to finally get closer to nature. But this dream quickly turns into a nightmare when it comes to the hostility of a changing peasant world. A brutal rejection that will profoundly mark the actor.

programme.title: Heritage of France
programme.desc: Every summer, the Roya Valley hosts a festival called "Passors of Humanity", several days of debates, exchanges and artistic performances to celebrate the mix of cultures and fraternity. Principles dear to this region, inherited from its past and unique geography.

programme.title: Public sense
programme.desc: The current issues and the major issues that drive the society are discussed by Thomas Hugues' guests. Experts, politicians or observers, they analyze the issues and compare their ideas to provide everyone with the keys to understanding the issues of the moment.

programme.title: France - Cambodia, so far, so close
programme.desc: How did Cambodia, ravaged less than fifty years ago by one of the most deadly genocides of the twentieth century, become the host of the 20th Summit of La Francophonie? And what remains, more than 160 years after the protectorate chosen by King Norodom I in 1863, of the singular bond between Phnom Penh and Paris? The common history of the two countries is that of a passionate relationship: a protectorate requested rather than impossibly, an independence obtained without confrontation by Norodom Sihanouk in 1953, and then the collapse under Pol Pot's regime. Peace is negotiated in Paris at the 1991 Conference. Those who have lived it from the inside tell behind the scenes. Cambodian officials are talking about reconstruction, the delicate balance between China, Vietnam and the West, and the place France can still hold.

programme.title: Second chance
programme.desc: In the famous health-care prison in the heart of Paris, inmates at the end of their sentence are undergoing an intensive rehabilitation and fight against recidivism. The scheme must help them prepare their CVs, interviews and a day of job dating, organized within the prison, in which a dozen employers who recruit will participate. At the key, maybe, a promise of employment. The documentary follows every stage of the Lamine and Oudiouma journey, until their first steps out of the walls.

programme.title: A world in doc
programme.desc: To question society, its fractures, its hopes, is the objective of the debate program "A world in doc". Rebecca Fitoussi moderates the discussion with specialists for half an hour to discuss and put into perspective a work broadcast just before.

programme.title: Tomorrow Havana
programme.desc: Asphyxiated by the embargo and paralyzed by an authoritarian and centralized system that struggles to reform, Cuba is going through one of the worst crises in its history. For the first time, five young Cubans agreed to tell their stories and to unveil their daily lives in Havana. In these exceptional stories and life slices, between the ruined buildings, the garbage that piles up, the water and electricity cuts, the endless lines in front of the shops and the constant surveillance of the State Security, is portrayed as an island with breathless breath where each struggles in his own way to get out of it.

programme.title: A particular brain
programme.desc: Chloe, Hajar, Geneviève and Ludovic are four HPI-detected adults. Some also have autism spectrum disorder or attention deficit disorder with or without hyperactivity. They are very different from each other, but they share the same feeling: that they have always lived in a time lag. Through their testimonies and feelings, they open the doors of their inner universe to understand what is being played in a neurodivergent brain. From sometimes chaotic journeys to the discovery of their functioning, they tell how this better self-knowledge has changed their gaze on their difference. To inform their experiences, researchers in neuroscience and psychology bring their eyes to better understand the mechanisms of this atypical functioning.

programme.title: On the mythical roads of France
programme.sub-title: The coast of the Iroise Sea with Philippe Lavil
programme.desc: In the company of singer Philippe Lavil, an exploration of a vibrant Brittany, from the wild coast of the Iroise Sea to the Monts d'Arrée, the cradle of many legends. This trip allows you to discover the island of Molène, long feared by sailors, before soaking up the dynamism of the city of Brest and then taking the direction of the Regional Natural Park of Armorique. Close to the Huelgoat forest, the encounter with an authentic Druid allows an unexpected dive into the heart of Breton culture.

programme.title: I hope it lasts.
programme.sub-title: How can we save our companies in trouble?
programme.desc:

programme.title: Heritage of France
programme.desc: The Fest noz, a Breton resistance. Between moors and green forests, the Breton countryside has been singing its history for millennia. In the Monts d'Arrée, in this Armo-American Brittany, the Fest Noz, or night singing, is much more than a popular song, it is a real trance that allows its followers to reconnect with the sky and the earth. - Dunkirk, when the carnival cry comes up. In Dunkirk, at the time of the carnival, the working-class districts, the bourgeois pavilions and the town hall with its belfry awaken and vibrate to the sound of a popular and joyful clamour.

programme.title: Parliament hebdo
programme.desc:

This season, a new formula: a debate between a Member of Parliament and a Senator on the major issues that are ripping the pace of Parliament's life.

programme.desc: In 2050, France will have nearly 5 million people over 85 years of age. Of these, 2.8 million are dependent. Are we ready to cope with the ageing population and dependency? Yet, the old age plan and its funding, announced since 2019, are still waiting. But the needs are considerable.

programme.title: Pier 8
programme.desc:
Karine Lacombe, a medical professor and first woman head of a hospital service for infectious diseases in Paris, was mediated during the crisis of the Covid-19. Today, she is practicing a caring medicine, centered on the patient's touch and listening. From student jobs to cyber-harassment she has been subjected to, she has never stopped fighting.
Presenter: Ali Rebeihi

programme.title: Pier 8
programme.desc:
Véronique Béchu, the police commander of the juvenile protection brigade and the Minors Office (OFMIN), is currently in police custody. She is dedicated to the association "e-Enfance", committed against online child crime. From "grooming" to sexual extortion, Véronique Béchu explains the explosion of content through the networking of criminals and the hyperconnection of children.
Presenter(s): Cécile Ollivier

programme.title: The Defence Journal
programme.desc: For more than two centuries, the semaphores have been watching. Silent sentinels, they are close to sixty today strategically marking the French coast. But the public often does not know that these vitarious silhouettes, which are located in the most beautiful coastal landscapes, are armed by the National Navy.

programme.title: The Defence Journal
programme.desc: Taking hostages, mined roads or discovery of shells dating from the Second World War, deminers intervene in various situations. Cold blood, precision and risk control are their main words. The armies are developing equipment to enhance their effectiveness and security in the field.

programme.title: Cannabis, a French paradox
programme.desc:
Today, more than one million French people use cannabis daily, even though the 1970 law on combating drug addiction and trafficking is one of the most repressive in the Western world. A real paradox that this documentary takes on through an investigation that explores the issue of cannabis in its legal, historical and social aspects.
Director(s): Ali Watani

programme.title: NCIS
programme.desc: A Marine was murdered. The investigations soon revealed that his attackers could be linked to a gang that Torres had investigated in the past.
programme.desc-more: In this exciting new season of NCIS, the team of specialized agents, led by the intrepid Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon), finds itself confronted with a series of complex and intriguing cases involving Navy personnel. Their investigation begins with the mysterious disappearance of a man, which occurred six months earlier, and which seems to be a crucial clue to a recent car explosion. As they explore this case, a new mystery arises: the tragic death of a woman whose body was found after a fall of a building. The victim's doctor, reluctant to share information about his or her background, becomes an issue for Gibbs, who must convince him or her to collaborate. Barely this resolved case, Gibbs, accompanied by Palmer (Brian Dietzen) and Quinn (Emily Wickersham), set out at sea to elucidate the murder of a marine, testing their ingenuity and determination. This 14th season promises to be rich in suspense and rebound.
